reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch argue Genesis 2 simply retells day six in closer focus, reading its verb for the animals as a pluperfect so no rival sequence exists.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen reads Genesis 1:27's emphasis on simultaneous male-and-female creation as a deliberate protest against the rival Genesis 2-3 account.

quotes.text: We cannot regard it as fortuitous that in this point Genesis i. asserts the opposite of Genesis ii. iii.; the words spoken with such emphasis, and repeated i. 27, v. 1, ix. 6, sound exactly like a protest against the view underlying Genesis ii. iii.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), ch. VIII.I, on Genesis 1:27 and Genesis 2-3.

sides.snippet: God created man in his own image. In God's image he created him; male and female he created them.
sides.verseText: God created man in his own image. In God's image he created him; male and female he created them.

sides.snippet: He made the rib, which Yahweh God had taken from the man, into a woman, and brought her to the man.
